archetype.name: Lottery Team (run-and-gun)
archetype.definition: A fast, three-happy team whose defense gives up too much at the rim and on the glass to stay out of the bottom five, and whose record matches its margin.

report.headline: A sieve at the rim, cold from three, and earning every loss
report.take:
Chicago is 4-12 and 26th of 30 on the site, and the record is honest. The W vs Pt Diff is only -1, and the margin implies five wins, so this is not a decent team losing close games. It is a below-average offense, 20th in ORtg at 112.2, paired with one of the league's worst defenses, 28th at 119.8. The 116.63 points a game, ninth in the league, flatter the attack. That number comes from a 102.6 pace well above the league's 98.5, not from efficiency. The same tempo turns the defense into the league's most generous at 124.56 allowed a game. Context matters too: the Bulls went 31-51 last season with a -5.1 Net Rtg, and it has been a steady slide down from 46-36 in 2021-22.

The defense breaks at one point: the paint. Opponents take 38.2% of their shots within four feet, worst in the league and far above the 29.6 league average. Once there, they finish at only 63.1%, ninth-best, so the Bulls contest rim shots fine but cannot keep anyone from getting there. They then fail to finish possessions. DRB% is 69.6, 28th, well below the 75.5 to 78.3 range of every season in the history block. They also force few turnovers, with Opp TOV % at 12.5, 24th. By position, point guards are torching them: 30.94 points a game allowed, 29th, and 5.3 over those players' own averages, last in the league. That points to point-of-attack defense that lets ball handlers turn the corner.

The numbers also hide some good news on offense. The Bulls take 45.9% of their shots from three, eighth in the league, but hit only 32.9%, 28th. Last season they hit 35.6% and the year before 36.7% on similar volume, so the shooting should come back toward normal. The roster's bright spot is Jalen Smith: ninth of 92 on the center tab, with a 66.6 TS % and a 3.1 BPM, both team bests. Matas Buzelis scores efficiently at 61 TS %. The bad news is availability. Norman Powell (271 points, 27.5 USG %) and Caleb Wilson (27.4 USG %) are both listed Out, which strips the two highest-usage creators. More minutes then go to Noa Essengue, last of 86 on his tab with a -8.1 BPM, and Zach Collins, at 38.9 TS %.

There is a real sign of life. The last five games went 2-3 with a +4 differential a game, almost 12 points better than the season norm. The defense allowed 117.6 a game over that stretch, after giving up 129.33 a game in October. That includes a 137-107 rout in Brooklyn and an 11-point win in Minnesota. It is a small sample built against mixed opposition, and it came partly before both injuries landed. Still, the direction is right, and a Bulls team that shoots like its recent history would be a 25-win-type club rather than a 21-win one.

strengths.title: Jalen Smith anchors the frontcourt
strengths.body: Smith is the one Bull ranking near the top of his position tab. He is efficient at 66.6 TS %, with a 3.1 BPM and a team-high 1.3 Win Shares, and he spaces the floor with 30 threes. His efficiency is built on shot selection rather than volume (18.9 USG %), which tends to hold up. Opponents' rim finishing is respectable partly because of him.

strengths.title: Three-point shooting due to rebound
strengths.body: The volume is there, eighth in 3PA Rate, but the 32.9% conversion ranks 28th and sits 2.5 points under the league. These are largely the same style of shots that went in at 36.7% two seasons ago. Expect the percentage to drift up, and with it an ORtg that currently ranks 20th.

strengths.title: Recent five games show real progress
strengths.body: Over the last five games the Bulls posted a +4 differential a game, nearly 12 points better than their season rate. The defense allowed 117.6 a game in that stretch. The tightening matches the month splits: October allowed 129.33 a game, November 121.7.

concerns.title: Paint access and defensive glass
concerns.body: Opponents get to the rim more often against Chicago than against any other team, and they grab their own misses at a rate that leaves the Bulls 28th in DRB %. Both numbers are far off the team's own history. That suggests a scheme or personnel problem, not noise, though some correction toward the past is plausible. Until it is fixed, the DRtg stays in the bottom three.

concerns.title: Two lead scorers out
concerns.body: Powell, the team's top scorer, and Wilson, its other high-usage option, are both listed Out. Their absence shifts creation onto Giddey, who shoots 51.7 TS %. It also opens minutes for Essengue, who sits at the bottom of the power-forward tab. All three roster groups already grade D or D+, so there is no depth to absorb this.

concerns.title: Point guards feast on them
concerns.body: Opposing point guards score 30.94 a game against Chicago, 29th in the league. They also hit 4.81 threes, last in the league, and outdo their own averages by more against Chicago than against anyone. This lines up with the paint-access problem: ball handlers turning the corner and either finishing or kicking out.

trend.note: A 1-5 October with a defense in freefall gave way to a more competitive November. The last five games came with a positive margin, though the record over the last ten is still 3-7.

weekAhead.headline: Cleveland at home, then two very winnable bottom-feeders
weekAhead.body:
The week opens with Cleveland, 12th on the site, owners of the fifth-best ORtg and a frontcourt graded A. They already beat Chicago 126-115 a week ago. With Chicago's rim and glass problems, that is the toughest game of the stretch. Cleveland's defense is only 20th, though, and it is soft on shooting guards and on centers stepping out for threes, which suits Smith.

Then come Charlotte (28th on the site) and Indiana (27th), two teams worse than or level with Chicago. Charlotte has the league's worst ORtg and eFG %, but it leads the league in ORB %. That is exactly where the Bulls bleed, so second-chance points will decide that game. Indiana is 26th in offense and is the league's weakest offensive rebounding team, which hides Chicago's flaw. A 2-1 week is realistic. 1-2 is the floor if the glass goes badly in Charlotte.

keyMatchups.title: Defensive glass versus Charlotte
keyMatchups.body: Charlotte rebounds 33.2% of its own misses, best in the league, against a Bulls team 28th in DRB %. Charlotte shoots terribly, so the only way its offense survives is extra possessions. If Chicago finishes possessions, it should win.

keyMatchups.title: Threes against leaky perimeters
keyMatchups.body: Charlotte allows 40% from three, last in the league, and Indiana's 37.4% ranks 26th. For a high-volume, cold-shooting team, these are the games for the percentage to snap back.

keyMatchups.title: Buzelis against Indiana's wings
keyMatchups.body: Indiana gives up 27.24 points a game to small forwards, the most in the league. Buzelis is Chicago's most efficient volume scorer among the healthy players. Against a Charlotte defense that allows the fewest points to centers, he is also the natural focal point with Smith walled off.

weekAhead.watch: Chicago's defensive rebounding in Charlotte: the clearest test of whether the recent defensive improvement is real.

restOfSeason.body:
The record matches the margin, so there is no luck to give back or collect. The path forward depends on two corrections. The first is three-point shooting moving back toward the mid-30s these Bulls hit in recent seasons. The second is a defensive rebounding rate that is unlikely to stay this far below anything the franchise has posted in the last five years. Both point up. Against that, Powell and Wilson are out, the roster groups all grade D-range, and the rim-access issue looks structural.

The current pace points to about 21 wins. Expect modestly better: a final total of 22 to 28 wins, an ORtg drifting toward league average as shots fall, and a DRtg that improves but stays bottom-five. This is a lottery team with a few watchable pieces, not a play-in team in waiting.
swingFactors: Return timeline for Powell and Wilson
Whether the defensive rebounding returns to its historical range

confidence.note: Sixteen games and injury-shifted rotations, but the record and margin agree.
